To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
grafted NSC can prevent the degenerative effects of 3‐NP in the host striatum.
grafted neural stem cells (gNSCs) can be deposited preventively into the CNS and can later shield the host environment from oxidative stress.
grafted NSC‐derived factors may prevent the degeneration and death of striatal neurons in vivo, in a model of chronic oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of endogenous NSC in the adult brain.
the development of a novel therapeutic strategy for the prevention of neurodegenerative disorders, which may involve the transplantation of grafted NSCs into the CNS.
the study of the mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective role of grafted NSCs in vivo and in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the grafted NSCs have a protective role in the host brain.
the grafted NSCs, by secreting neuroprotective factors and by providing an antioxidant environment, can prevent the degenerative process of the host striatum.
grafted NSC may have a dual function, i.e., they may rescue neurons in a damaged brain and may also protect neurons from oxidative stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
grafted NSC can protect the host environment from oxidative stress, which is the main cause of the degeneration and death of the neurons.
NSCs can protect the host environment from oxidative stress, thus preventing the degeneration of the host neurons.
NSCs may act as a “biological shield” for the host CNS, and this may be particularly relevant in neurodegenerative diseases, where the CNS may be particularly susceptible to oxidative stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grafted NSC‐like cells can protect the CNS from oxidative stress.
the transplantation of NSCs into the intact brain may be beneficial to the host environment, and may be used for preventive purposes.
grafted NSC may be a promising therapeutic strategy for the prevention and treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
